variables.subject: marmot.jpg
variables.shot_1_establish:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the cartoon marmot in <Picture 1>: standing upright on its hind legs at a chrome microphone on a boom stand, its fur banded brown and cream with dark mask-like patches around the eyes, a pale muzzle, long white whiskers and alert rounded ears.
<Picture 1> is a subject and setting reference only. It establishes who <Subject 1> is - fur, face, build and the microphone it sings into - and the club around it, its stage dressing, haze, warm amber light and the guitar in soft focus. It carries no compositional detail: no framing, no shot size, no camera position, no camera height and no lens. The composition of this clip is the one described below and is not taken from <Picture 1>.
<Audio 1> is the piece of the song covering this part of the video, a slow jazz number <Subject 1> sings into the microphone.

summary:
[image reference + audio song reference] The target video is a wide establishing shot of the whole stage, <Subject 1> small in the frame at its microphone, in one continuous shot.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the fur banding, eye patches, muzzle, whiskers, ears and proportions of <Picture 1> are kept exactly, with the head, jaw and shoulders newly animated to sing.
<Picture 1>: partially_copy - identity, wardrobe, set, palette and lighting are taken from it; framing, shot size, camera position, camera height and lens are NOT. This clip is a wide establishing shot taking in the whole stage, with <Subject 1> occupying roughly a third of the frame height, which is deliberately different from the framing of <Picture 1>.
<Audio 1>: partially_copy - the piece of the song covering this part of the video is reused as the soundtrack. <Subject 1>'s mouth is synchronised to the sung voice in it and to nothing else: the instrumental parts drive no mouth movement at all. Where the recording plays without a voice - an intro, a fill, a rest between phrases - <Subject 1> waits at the microphone with its mouth shut. Where a voice sings, the mouth, jaw and throat follow its timing and phrasing exactly.

detailed_description:
The target video is in the warmly lit, softly rendered cartoon style of <Picture 1>. [Shot 1] A wide shot takes in the whole small stage: the deep maroon curtain across the back, the acoustic guitar on its stand at frame right, the keyboard at frame left, amber light raking through haze. <Subject 1> stands centre frame at the microphone, full body visible from the feet up and occupying about a third of the frame height, with empty stage on either side of it. Its mouth is driven entirely by the vocal of <Audio 1>: it opens and moves only while a voice is actually singing, and stays completely closed - lips together, jaw still - through every instrumental passage, rest and gap between phrases, however long one runs. It never mimes, hums or chews when no voice is present, and it never holds still while a voice is singing. Between phrases it listens, the eyes staying open and blinking at a natural rate. The lighting, colour and contrast match <Picture 1> exactly and are steady from the first frame to the last, with smooth fur and no grain, speckle or hardened edges. The camera holds this framing statically throughout, with no reframing, no zoom and no cut.

overall_soundscape:
The song of <Audio 1> carries the shot, the vocal close and warm at the microphone. Under it, a low crowd murmur well back in the room and the faint hum of the stage amplifiers.

non_diegetic_music:
None - the music is the diegetic performance of <Audio 1>.
